run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The hotel-reservation namespace was (re)created inside the authorised window: all 19 pods were created 01:26:26–01:26:42Z, are Running/Ready with restartCount 0, and their start-up, DB-init and Consul-registration logs are clean (no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff or probe-failure events). Sampled traces from 01:26:44–01:26:58Z are healthy: HTTP GET /hotels, HTTP POST /reservation (10/10 sampled = http.status_code 200), /search.Search/Nearby, /rate.Rate/GetRates, /geo.Geo/Nearby, /profile.Profile/GetProfiles and /user.User/CheckUser all returned without error status and with millisecond latencies. The concrete fault found in the deployed state is a frontend Service/Endpoint mismatch: the search Deployment's pod template (and its pod) carries the label service-route=frontend, which is exactly the selector of the 'frontend' Service, so the 'frontend' Endpoints contain two addresses on port 5000 — the frontend pod (10.244.125.30) and the search pod (10.244.234.165) — while the search container only exposes 8082/9092 and registers itself as srv-search at 10.244.234.165:8082. No process in the search pod listens on 5000, so traffic the Service balances to it is refused. The label was added to the search pod template by manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 01:26:41Z (new ReplicaSet search-9cd459687 with the label replaced search-567bb6c4b8 without it; the superseded search pod was deleted at 01:26:42Z). The same manager added the label to the frontend Deployment at 01:26:39Z, which is required for the frontend pod to be selected at all, so the anomaly is the label on search. Direct evidence of failed client requests is missing: the frontend logs no per-request lines, the sampled traces contain no error-status spans for this path (a refused connection produces no span), there are no Ingress objects, the client path is unknown, and the window holds only ~35 s of application runtime, so no baseline exists. Two further observations are non-impact: the app-metrics scrape targets rate.hotel-reservation:9091 and search.hotel-reservation:9092 report up=0, and blackbox probe_success is 0 for every target in the cluster, including namespaces with no pods, making those probes unusable. The alternative candidate — the failure-admin-geo/failure-admin-rate revocation scripts mounted into mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate — is rejected: both mongo logs show the init script granting readWrite to admin (01:26:31Z rate-db, 01:26:34Z geo-db), geo/rate generated test data and served requests successfully at 01:26:58Z, and no later local (127.0.0.1) admin authentication or revoke output appears in either mongo log.

claims.text: The search Deployment's pod template labels are {io.kompose.service: search, service-route: frontend}, and the resulting pod search-9cd459687-dfhss also carries service-route=frontend; the frontend pod frontend-5566ddfbfb-sxt8n carries {io.kompose.service: frontend, service-route: frontend}.

The Service 'frontend' (ClusterIP 10.96.149.219, port 5000) has selector {service-route: frontend}, whereas every other hotel-reservation Service (geo, rate, search, ...) selects io.kompose.service=<name>.

The Endpoints of Service 'frontend' list two ready addresses on port 5000: 10.244.125.30 (frontend-5566ddfbfb-sxt8n) and 10.244.234.165 (search-9cd459687-dfhss), i.e. the search pod is registered behind the frontend Service on port 5000.

The search container exposes only containerPort 8082 and 9092 (the frontend container exposes 5000), and the search process registered itself in Consul as 'srv-search' at 10.244.234.165:8082 — the same pod IP that the frontend Service publishes on port 5000, so that endpoint has no listener on 5000.

The service-route=frontend label on search was introduced at 01:26:41Z: Deployment 'search' is generation 2 with a last write by manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 2026-11-24T01:26:41Z, the new ReplicaSet search-9cd459687 (created 01:26:41Z) has the service-route=frontend template label while the superseded ReplicaSet search-567bb6c4b8 (created 01:26:28Z) does not.

Kubernetes events for that rollout: Deployment 'search' "Scaled up replica set search-9cd459687 from 0 to 1" at 01:26:41Z, pod search-9cd459687-dfhss created/started 01:26:41Z, ReplicaSet search-567bb6c4b8 "Deleted pod: search-567bb6c4b8-hznv4" and Deployment "Scaled down replica set search-567bb6c4b8 from 1 to 0" at 01:26:42Z; the analogous label change on Deployment 'frontend' was written by manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 01:26:39Z.

Deployments 'frontend' and 'search' both kept the same pod-template image digest (ghcr.io/sregym/hotel-reservation:sha-d2c036bc3d...@sha256:1c685e1c...), i.e. both rollouts were label-only (config) changes, not new code.

All 19 hotel-reservation pods are phase Running and Ready with restartCount 0 (including search-9cd459687-dfhss and frontend-5566ddfbfb-sxt8n); hotel-reservation events in the window contain no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff or Failed phases — only Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started, two FailedMount warnings during startup, and the frontend/search rollout Killing events.

A representative complete trace (2eba58b9698f682c, 01:26:58Z) shows HTTP GET /hotels with http.status_code=200 and healthy children: frontend /search.Search/Nearby 4272us, search /geo.Geo/Nearby 516us and /rate.Rate/GetRates 3252us, geo /geo.Geo/Nearby 45us, rate /rate.Rate/GetRates 2531us, reservation CheckAvailability 448us, profile GetProfiles 238us, plus memcached client spans; no span carries an error status.

All 10 sampled HTTP POST /reservation traces on frontend (spans 01:26:44.66Z–01:26:58.81Z) returned http.status_code=200, with reservation /reservation.Reservation/MakeReservation 1557–8282us and user /user.User/CheckUser 21–53us; no error rows.

mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate both ran their init scripts inside the window and granted readWrite to admin and root on geo-db / rate-db ("Granting readWrite role to admin on rate-db database..." 01:26:31Z, geo-db 01:26:34Z); geo then logged "Generating test data... Successfull" at 01:26:36Z and rate at 01:26:33Z, and no later 127.0.0.1 admin authentication or revoke/Downgrading line appears in either mongo log through the end of the window.

geo, rate, reservation, profile and user application logs contain no runtime error/panic/refused/timeout lines beyond startup messages, and the only frontend stderr lines matching error/refused in the window are startup 'consul ... connect: connection refused' lines written at 01:26:27Z by the superseded pod frontend-68745cb99c-7g4cs before Consul was up.

At evaluation time 01:26:59Z the Prometheus scrape targets rate.hotel-reservation:9091 and search.hotel-reservation:9092 (job hotel-reservation-application) report up=0, while the blackbox targets frontend.hotel-reservation:5000, geo.hotel-reservation:8083, rate.hotel-reservation:8084 and search.hotel-reservation:8082 report up=1.

blackbox probe_success is 0 for every hotel-reservation target at 01:26:59Z and stayed 0 for all samples from 01:25:00Z to 01:26:45Z, but it is also 0 for all astronomy-shop and social-network targets and the ingress URL even though no astronomy-shop/social-network pods and no Ingress objects exist in this cluster; the blackbox probe results are therefore not usable as evidence about hotel-reservation health.

Because the frontend Service load-balances port 5000 over both the frontend pod and the search pod and the search pod has no listener on 5000, the requests the Service sends to the search pod are refused (connection reset), so clients using the 'frontend' Service see intermittent failures on /hotels, /recommendations, /reservation and /user. This is inferred from the endpoint/port mismatch; it is not directly observed, because a refused connection produces no server span or log line and no 5xx status appeared in the sampled traces.

A revoked MongoDB privilege was considered as the cause because ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo (revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh, TARGET_DB=geo-db) and failure-admin-rate (revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh, TARGET_DB=rate-db) are mounted at /scripts in mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate and those two Deployments were re-rolled with the mount at 01:26:29Z/01:26:30Z. It is rejected: neither mongo log shows any revokeRolesFromUser/Downgrading output or any local admin authentication after the init grant, and geo, rate and reservation served successful reads/writes afterwards (geo/rate DB sessions and test-data generation succeeded at 01:26:33–01:26:36Z, and /geo.Geo/Nearby, /rate.Rate/GetRates and MakeReservation returned without error at 01:26:58Z).

Remove the service-route=frontend label from the search Deployment's pod template (and from the running search pod) so that the 'frontend' Service only selects the frontend pod; alternatively narrow the 'frontend' Service selector to io.kompose.service=frontend like every other Service in the namespace. Then re-check the Service's endpoints to confirm only the frontend pod on port 5000 remains.

gaps: No direct evidence of failed frontend requests exists in the sampled data: the frontend container logs no per-request lines, the sampled traces contain no 5xx or error-status spans (a connection refused by the search pod yields no span), and the trace view is a biased recent sample, so the actual client failure rate of the frontend Service is unverified.

The application has only ~35 s of runtime inside the authorised window (pods created 01:26:26–01:26:42Z), so there is no comparable baseline and no pre/post-change comparison for any latency or error signal.

No Ingress objects exist anywhere in the cluster and the client-side load generator is not a pod in this cluster, so the exact path by which /hotels traffic reaches the frontend Service (and therefore how much of it is affected) is unknown.

Whether the failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate scripts were ever executed cannot be verified from pod logs (a kubectl-exec stream would not appear in the container log) and the change-history integration is not connected in this Run; the absence of any revoke argument in mongo logs is the only check performed.

A query for the rate service's own metric series (rate_requests_received_total range query, and the rate_* instant query) returned no samples (status no_data), matching the rate container's down metrics target; therefore rate_queue_depth, rate_requests_rejected_total, rate_requests_expired_total, rate_in_flight and rate_backend_qps_limit could not be evaluated.

No per-pod or per-node connection-refusal/reset counter was identified or checked (metric names such as container_network_receive_packets_total and node_netstat_Tcp_* exist), so the hypothesised refused connections on the search pod's port 5000 are not counted anywhere.
The trace sampling view delivered as evidence (4f244f2c-30c6-48e6-b630-c665d61e9c66-t0) was truncated at 60 of 171 rows, so the unsampled remainder of that window was not reviewed.
next_steps: Have a human confirm whether the search Deployment was intended to carry service-route=frontend; if not, revert that label in the pod template and verify the frontend Service endpoints afterwards.
Compare the client-side success rate / 5xx counts of the frontend Service before and after the 01:26:41Z search rollout using the load generator's own metrics (not available in this Run).

Investigate why rate.hotel-reservation:9091 and search.hotel-reservation:9092 are not scrapeable and why blackbox probe_success is 0 cluster-wide, since those signals cannot currently be used for alerting.

Check the failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate scripts against the mongo logs at a later time to determine whether the admin readWrite revoke was ever applied, as it is the other plausible fault in this scenario family.
